description: Ed25519 signatures over embedded labels and encrypted URLs

cases.description: Sign an embedded label: JCS of the label without `signature`, after the domain prefix
Signing ignores an existing `signature` member, so re-signing gives the same token
Sign an encrypted URL: its exact bytes, then `&sig=` is appended
Percent-encoding in the path is signed exactly as written
JCS sorts member names by UTF-16 code units, not code points: U+1F344 (surrogates D83C DF44) sorts before U+FB01
JCS string escaping: only `"`, `\\`, and control characters are escaped (short forms where they exist, else lowercase \u00xx); `/`, U+2028, DEL, and non-ASCII are literal UTF-8
JCS numbers use the ECMAScript Number-to-String rules on IEEE 754 doubles: 1.0 is 1, -0 is 0, 1e21 is 1e+21, integers above 2^53 round to the nearest double
A label signed by a trusted kid verifies
Member order and whitespace don't matter: the verifier canonicalizes the parsed label
String escapes don't matter: \u0050leurotus and \/ parse to the same values
Verifies the key-order label from members in a different order
Verifies the string label written with different escapes
Verifies the number label written with different number spellings
JCS does not normalize Unicode: the same name in NFD form is different bytes
A changed top-level field fails verification
A changed nested field fails verification
An added field fails verification
A removed field fails verification
A number replaced with the equal string fails verification
Edited and re-signed with a key that isn't in the trust store (its public key is even embedded in the label): the verifier ignores the embedded key
Edited and re-signed with an untrusted key that claims a trusted kid fails verification
Signed by one trusted key, labelled with another trusted kid: fails verification
The kid is part of the signed bytes: replacing it with another kid for the same key fails
A label without `signature` is unsigned, not invalid
A pre-1.4.0 `signature` string that isn't a 1.4.0 token is malformed, never valid
Malformed signature token (padding)
Malformed signature token (non-base64url-character)
Malformed signature token (short)
Malformed signature token (long)
Malformed signature token (non-canonical-bits)
Malformed signature token (no-kid)
Malformed signature token (empty-kid)
Malformed signature token (kid-bad-character)
Malformed signature token (kid-too-long)
Malformed signature token (extra-dot)
Malformed signature token (whitespace)
A `signature` that isn't a string is malformed
A label with a lone surrogate isn't I-JSON and can't be canonicalized
A label that isn't a JSON object is malformed
Verifiers MUST reject S >= L (RFC 8032 section 5.1.7): S + L is a malleated copy
A signature taken from a signed URL doesn't verify on an embedded label
A signature over the canonical JSON without the domain prefix fails verification
A signature made with the encrypted-url prefix doesn't verify as embedded
A signature over a label with field-level encryption covers the encrypted objects as printed, and verifies without any decryption key
Changing an encrypted field object fails verification
A signed pbkdf2 URL verifies
A signed raw-key URL verifies
A signed URL with a percent-encoded ID verifies
Verifiers don't re-normalize: %2F rewritten as %2f decodes the same but fails
A changed ciphertext fails verification
A changed `i` fails verification
A changed ID path segment fails verification
Parameter order is part of the signed bytes: swapping `e` and `iv` fails
A parameter added before `sig` fails verification
`sig` MUST be the last parameter
`sig` MUST appear once
The token is never percent-decoded
A signed URL with a fragment is malformed
A signed URL must be ASCII (non-ASCII is percent-encoded)
Only `wemush://v1/encrypted/` URLs can be verified
A URL re-signed with a key not in the trust store
Signed by one trusted key, labelled with another trusted kid
A URL without `sig` is unsigned
The reserved 1.3.1 `sig` value (64 bytes, no kid) is malformed, never valid
A padded signature is malformed
Cross-form replay: an embedded label's signature doesn't verify on a URL
A signature over the URL bytes made with the embedded prefix fails verification
Duplicate member names make the text malformed, even without a signature
A duplicate member name in a nested object is malformed, even without a signature
A signed label with a duplicate top-level member name is malformed, not valid or invalid
A signed label with a duplicate nested member name is malformed
Member names are compared after unescaping: `stage` and `\u0073tage` are duplicates
A lone surrogate makes the text malformed, even without a signature
`NaN` isn't JSON, so the text is malformed, even without a signature
A number that overflows a double (1e400) isn't I-JSON: malformed, even without a signature
Text that isn't JSON at all is malformed (it has no URI scheme, so it takes the JSON rules)
Signers MUST refuse an encrypted URL with no query
Signers MUST refuse an encrypted URL with an empty query
Signers MUST refuse a URL that already has `sig`; remove it before re-signing
Signers MUST refuse label text with duplicate member names
Signers MUST refuse label text with a lone surrogate

A trust-store entry with a 32-byte key that doesn't decode to an Ed25519 point is a configuration error. If it reaches verification the result is invalid, not unknown-kid; rejecting the entry when the trust store is built also conforms
A trust-store entry with a 31-byte key is a configuration error. If it reaches verification the result is invalid, not unknown-kid; rejecting the entry when the trust store is built also conforms

A trust-store entry with an algorithm other than Ed25519 is a configuration error. If it reaches verification the result is invalid, not unknown-kid; rejecting the entry when the trust store is built also conforms
A key set with two Ed25519 keys loads both, and a label signed by one verifies
Entries with algorithms the implementation doesn't support are skipped, not errors; the remaining Ed25519 key still verifies
A skipped entry's other members aren't checked: no kid, a bad kid, or no publicKey is fine
Duplicate kids are checked only among usable entries: a skipped entry may share a kid with an Ed25519 entry
`alg` is compared exactly: `ed25519` isn't a supported algorithm, so the entry is skipped and the label's kid is unknown
A key set with no keys loads as an empty trust store
Members the specification doesn't define are ignored
An Ed25519 entry with 32 bytes that aren't a curve point is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a 31-byte key is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a 33-byte key is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a padded base64url key is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a key with unused bits set is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with no publicKey is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a publicKey that isn't a string is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with no kid is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a kid outside the token's kid syntax is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a 65-character kid is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
An Ed25519 entry with a kid that isn't a string is a configuration error: loading fails, rather than dropping the key
Two Ed25519 entries with the same kid are a configuration error
A repeated kid is a configuration error even when both entries carry the same key
A key set document that is an array is a configuration error
A key set document that is a string is a configuration error
A key set document that is null is a configuration error
A key set document that is an object without `keys` is a configuration error
A key set document that is an object whose `keys` isn't an array is a configuration error
A key set document that is a `keys` element that isn't an object is a configuration error
A key set document that is an entry without `alg` is a configuration error
A key set document that is an entry whose `alg` isn't a string is a configuration error
Sign-then-encrypt, last step: sign an encrypted URL whose plaintext is a signed embedded label (the `sign-embedded` label and token)
Sign-then-encrypt: the URL signature verifies, the URL decrypts to a signed embedded label, and that label's own signature verifies after decryption
A signed encrypted URL whose plaintext has no `signature`: outer valid, inner unsigned
`i` changed after signing: the outer signature fails, which a scanner can see before spending PBKDF2 work. Decryption also fails, because the derived key changes

The plaintext re-encrypted under the same passphrase with another IV, keeping the old `sig`: `e` and `iv` changed, so the outer signature fails, but the inner signature still verifies, because it covers the plaintext
The embedded label was changed after it was signed, then encrypted and the URL signed: the outer signature is valid, and the inner signature is invalid

Domain separation: the inner (`embedded`) token copied into the URL's `sig`. Its kid is trusted, but it was signed in the `embedded` domain, so the outer signature is invalid. The inner signature still verifies
